title.narrative: Tanzania Human Rights Defenders Coalition THRDC 2023-2025
Tanzania Human Rights Defenders Coalition THRDC 2023-2025

description.narrative:
Tanzania Human Rights Defenders Coalition (THRDC) is a non-governmental membership organisation registered under the NGO act. It has grown in importance since it was first formed 2012 and now comprises of almost 250 member organisations. THRDC is a strong player for Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) and has been able to build links with key national government institutions such as the Commission of Human Rights and Good Governance (CHRAGG), Registrar of NGO:s, police force and the legislature.
The main goal of THRDC is to enhance security and protection of the HRDs in Tanzania and to create a safer working environment. It also intends to strengthen regional and international interventions towards protection and promotion of the rights and responsibilities of the HRDs.
The Strategic Plan for 2023-2027 focus on three key results areas:
a. Preventive protection and security management: Assurance of preventive protection and security management of HRDs (who are at potential risks). b. Members empowerment and public engagement: Strengthen THRDC members and other stakeholders capacities and resilience. c. THRDCs institutional sustenance: Improvement of institutional performance and sustainability.

Tanzania Human Rights Defenders Coalition (THRDC) är en icke-statlig medlemsorganisation och registrerad NGO. Koalitionen har vuxit i betydelse sedan den först bildades 2012 och består nu av nästan 250 medlemsorganisationer. THRDC är en stark aktör för människorättsförsvarare och har kunnat bygga broar med viktiga nationella regeringsinstitutioner som Commission of Human Rights and Good Governance (CHRAGG), registrator of NGO:s, polisen och rättsväsendet.
Det huvudsakliga målet för THRDC är att förbättra säkerheten och skyddet av människorättsförsvarare i Tanzania och att skapa en säkrare arbetsmiljö för dessa. De avser också att stärka regionala och internationella insatser för att skydda och främja människors rättigheter och skyldigheter.

Some examples of THRDCs work and results 2024: Aiming to increase HRDs recognition at various levels and influencing reforms in favor of HRDs, THRDC engaged in advocacy at various levels including 4 engagements with African human rights mechanisms, 5 engagements with UN human rights mechanisms and engaged in 6 different legal reforms processes. Further, THRDC released 21 press statements, conducted 13 joint interventions with various other CSO actors and delivered 12 different publications on the Coalitions interventions and the situation of HRDs in Tanzania, to mention a few. THRDC broadened its membership base by adding 28 new members totaling 285 members (organisations), which has a significant impact in promoting human rights in different zones and largely at the national level. In addition, THRDC have established a Domestic Resources Mobilization Committee and Strategy.
Through the work of THRDC: - The people of Ngorogoro reclaimed their forfeited constitutional rights - Contributed to amendments of the Finance Act of 2024, which expanded the definition of charitable status to include organisations working on environmental and health issues - HRDs and media outlets provided with legal support have continued with their human rights work without fear after winning cases that aimed to deregister them and cases that could lead to prison sentence. - 245 HRDs were supported with protection services, of which among them have saved lives of two HRDs (confidential info) A committee was formed by the government to investigate human rights violations (killings) in Serengeti after THRDC through Watetezi TV released a documentary over inhumane acts done by the Tanzania National Parks Authority officers over the people. However, there are many challenges: the existence of suppressive laws i.e. Basic Rights and Duties Enforcement Act (BRADEA), arrests and prosecution, limited resources for the Coalition and its members which hinders the implementation of planned work, limited capacity (and resources) of most grassroot member organisations, etc.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
